section_title: Punishment for murder — Death Penalty jurisprudence
section_desc: Under Section 302 IPC, death penalty is reserved for the rarest of rare cases (Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, 1980). The court must weigh aggravating and mitigating circumstances. Aggravating: pre-planned, heinous, involving vulnerable victims, multiple murders. Mitigating: young age, mental illness, first offender, provocation. Life imprisonment is the rule; death penalty is the exception.

For criminal conspiracy under Section 120A IPC, the prosecution must prove: (1) two or more persons; (2) an agreement; (3) the agreement is to do or cause to be done an illegal act or a lawful act by illegal means. No overt act is required except for conspiracies not involving a substantive offence. Mere knowledge of conspiracy is not sufficient — active participation must be proved.

Section 304B IPC: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs under abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, and it is shown that she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry — such death shall be called 'dowry death'. The husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused such death. Punishment: imprisonment for not less than seven years, may extend to life.

Section 420 IPC requires: (1) deception of any person; (2) dishonest or fraudulent inducement; (3) delivery of property or causing an act. Important: the deception must be of a fact (not mere opinion). The dishonest intent must exist from the beginning. Mere breach of contract does not constitute cheating. If promise of payment is made without intent to pay at the time of making the promise, it constitutes cheating.

section_title: Cruelty by husband — Elements and bail
section_desc: Section 498A IPC punishes cruelty by husband or relatives of husband. Cruelty includes: (a) conduct likely to drive woman to suicide or cause grave injury to health; (b) harassment with a view to coercing her or her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for property/dowry. The offence is cognizable, non-bailable, non-compoundable (though SC has allowed compounding in some cases). SC in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar directed police not to arrest mechanically.

Section 41 CrPC: Police officer may arrest without warrant when person commits cognizable offence in presence of officer; when person is proclaimed offender; when possession of stolen property; when obstructs police officer. As per Arnesh Kumar judgment (2014), police must record reasons before arrest; magistrate must apply mind before remand. Sections 41A-41D: notice of appearance, right to counsel, inspection memo during arrest.

Section 161 CrPC: Police may examine any person acquainted with the facts of the case. Such statement is recorded in writing. The statement under Section 161 is not on oath and is not admissible as substantive evidence in trial — it can only be used to contradict or corroborate the witness under Section 145 of Indian Evidence Act. Such statements shall not be signed by the person making them.
chapter_title: Information to the Police and their Powers to Investigate

section_desc: Section 164 CrPC: A Magistrate may record any confession or statement made to him in the course of an investigation. Before recording, the Magistrate must warn the person that he is not bound to make a confession, and if he does so, it may be used as evidence. The person must be given time to reflect. The Magistrate shall record that he gave the warning and is satisfied that the confession is voluntary. Such confessions are admissible as evidence.
chapter_title: Information to the Police and their Powers to Investigate

section_title: Report of police officer on completion of investigation (charge sheet)
section_desc: Section 173 CrPC: After completion of investigation, the officer in charge of the police station shall forward a report (charge sheet/final report) to the Magistrate. The charge sheet must contain: names of parties, nature of information, names of persons acquainted with circumstances, whether offence appears to have been committed, name of accused if known and arrested. Filing charge sheet leads to cognizance by court.
chapter_title: Information to the Police and their Powers to Investigate

section_desc: Section 197 CrPC: No Court shall take cognizance of any offence alleged to have been committed by any member of the armed forces of the Union or by any person who is or was a Judge, Magistrate or public servant not removable from his office save by or with the sanction of the Government. The purpose is to protect public servants acting in good faith from frivolous prosecutions.
chapter_title: Conditions Requisite for Initiation of Proceedings

section_desc: Section 313 CrPC: The court shall examine the accused for the purpose of enabling him personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidence against him. The examination under Section 313 is not on oath, and the accused's statement cannot be treated as evidence, but the court may consider it. Adverse inference can be drawn for false answers or evasions.

Section 374 CrPC: Any person convicted on a trial held by a High Court in its extraordinary original criminal jurisdiction may appeal to the Supreme Court. Any person convicted on a trial held by a Sessions Judge or an Additional Sessions Judge or on a trial held by any other court in which a sentence of imprisonment for more than seven years has been passed may appeal to the High Court. Any person convicted on a trial held by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Magistrate of First Class, Second Class may appeal to Sessions Court.

section_title: Courts to try all civil suits unless barred
section_desc: Section 9 CPC: The courts shall have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred. A suit is of civil nature if it is primarily a suit for enforcement of a civil right or is for relief of a civil wrong. A suit is not of civil nature if it relates to a political question or caste question involving no civil right.

section_title: Other suits to be instituted where defendant resides or where cause of action arises
section_desc: Section 20 CPC: Subject to the limitations aforesaid, every suit shall be instituted in a court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant, or each of the defendants where there are more than one, at the time of the commencement of the suit, actually and voluntarily resides, or carries on business, or personally works for gain; or in the case of a body corporate, where it has its principal office; or where the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises.

Section 26 CPC: Every suit shall be instituted by presentation of a plaint. A plaint must contain: name of court; name and description of plaintiff; name and description of defendant; facts constituting cause of action; relief claimed; value of suit for jurisdiction. Order VII CPC governs contents of a plaint. An affidavit must accompany the plaint.

section_title: Questions to be determined by court executing decree
section_desc: Section 47 CPC: All questions arising between the parties to the suit in which the decree was passed, or their representatives, and relating to the execution, discharge, or satisfaction of the decree, shall be determined by the court executing the decree and not by a separate suit. This prevents multiplicity of suits on execution matters.

Section 80 CPC: No suit shall be instituted against the Government or against a public officer in respect of any act purporting to be done by such public officer in his official capacity, until the expiration of two months next after notice in writing has been delivered to or left at the office of the appropriate Government authority. The notice must state the cause of action, name and address of the plaintiff, relief claimed.

Section 96 CPC: Save where otherwise expressly provided in the body of this Code or by any other law for the time being in force, an appeal shall lie from every decree passed by any court exercising original jurisdiction to the court authorised to hear appeals from the decisions of such court. No appeal shall lie from a decree passed by the court with the consent of parties.

Order 39 CPC: The court may by order grant a temporary injunction to restrain any person from committing breach of contract or other injury of any kind before the hearing of the suit or at any stage of the proceedings, if it appears that the object of granting the relief would be defeated by the delay. Conditions: prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable injury. The court may also order for appointment of receiver.

Order 40 CPC: It shall be lawful for the court to appoint a receiver of any property before or after decree on such terms as to the court seem just, to remove any person from the possession or custody of the property; to commit the property to the custody of such officer as the court thinks fit; to grant to such receiver all such powers as to bringing and defending suits and for the realization, management, protection, preservation and improvement of the property.

section_title: Confession to police officer — Not admissible
section_desc: Section 25 IEA: No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence. This absolute bar is to prevent police torture. Even if the accused voluntarily confesses to police, it is inadmissible. Exception: If the confession leads to discovery of facts (Section 27 IEA), only the part of the statement that distinctly relates to the discovered fact is admissible.

section_title: How much of information received from accused may be proved
section_desc: Section 27 IEA: Provided that, when any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from a person accused of any offence, in the custody of a police officer, so much of such information, whether it amounts to a confession or not, as relates distinctly to the fact thereby discovered, may be proved. This is an exception to Sections 25 and 26.

section_title: Cases in which statement of relevant fact by person who is dead or cannot be found is relevant — Dying Declaration
section_desc: Section 32 IEA: Statements, written or verbal, of relevant facts made by a person who is dead, or who cannot be found, or who has become incapable of giving evidence, or whose attendance cannot be procured without an amount of delay or expense which under the circumstances appears unreasonable, are themselves relevant facts — especially dying declarations (sub-section 1). A dying declaration is admissible even without corroboration if the court is satisfied it is truthful.
chapter_title: Statements by Persons who Cannot be Called as Witnesses

section_desc: Section 45 IEA: When the court has to form an opinion upon a point of foreign law, or of science, or art, or as to identity of handwriting or finger impressions, the opinions upon that point of persons specially skilled in such foreign law, science, art, or in questions as to identity of handwriting or finger impressions are relevant facts. Expert opinions include medical, forensic, handwriting, ballistics, digital forensics experts.
chapter_title: Opinion of Third Persons When Relevant

section_desc: Section 65B IEA: Any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be also a document and shall be admissible in any proceedings without further proof of production of the original. Certificate under Section 65B(4) is required to authenticate electronic evidence. In Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal (2020), the Supreme Court held that the 65B certificate is mandatory.

Section 101 IEA: Whoever desires any court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts which he asserts, must prove that those facts exist. When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person. In criminal cases, the prosecution bears the burden to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. In civil cases, the burden is to prove on preponderance of probabilities.

section_title: Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecutions for rape
section_desc: Section 114A IEA: In a prosecution for rape under clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g) of sub-section (2) of section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, where sexual intercourse by the accused is proved and the question is whether it was without the consent of the woman alleged to have been raped and such woman states in her evidence before the court that she did not consent, the court shall presume that she did not consent.

section_title: Dishonour of cheque — essentials and procedure
section_desc: Section 138 NIA: For conviction under Section 138, the following must be proved: (1) cheque drawn for legally enforceable debt; (2) cheque presented within validity (3 months); (3) cheque dishonoured; (4) legal notice given within 30 days of dishonour; (5) drawer fails to pay within 15 days of notice. Complaint to be filed within 30 days of expiry of 15-day notice period. Trial by Magistrate, summary trial possible. Punishment: imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to twice cheque amount, or both.

Section 139 NIA: It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque in the discharge of, wholly or in part, any debt or other liability. This presumption is rebuttable. The accused can rebut this by showing preponderance of probabilities that no legally enforceable debt existed. Once the accused provides a plausible defence, the burden shifts back to complainant.

section_title: Conditions for a Hindu marriage — detailed
section_desc: Section 5 HMA: A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus, if: (i) neither party has a spouse living at the time; (ii) neither party is of unsound mind or incapable of giving valid consent; (iii) the bridegroom has completed age of 21 years and bride has completed age of 18 years; (iv) the parties are not within the degrees of prohibited relationship unless custom permits; (v) the parties are not sapindas of each other unless custom permits.

Section 13 HMA: Grounds for divorce: (1) adultery; (2) cruelty; (3) desertion for 2 years; (4) conversion to another religion; (5) unsound mind for 3 years; (6) virulent and incurable leprosy; (7) venereal disease in communicable form; (8) renouncing the world; (9) not heard alive for 7 years. Additional grounds for wife: husband's bigamy; rape, sodomy or bestiality; non-resumption of cohabitation for one year after maintenance order; repudiation of marriage (Option of Puberty).

Section 13B HMA: A petition for dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce may be presented to the district court by both parties together on the ground that they have been living separately for a period of one year or more, that they have not been able to live together and that they have mutually agreed that the marriage should be dissolved. On motion of one party or both after 6 to 18 months of first motion, if not withdrawn, the court shall pass decree of divorce.

Order 21 CPC: Modes of execution of money decree: (1) delivery of property; (2) attachment and sale of property; (3) arrest and detention of judgment debtor (civil prison); (4) appointment of receiver; (5) in such other manner as nature of relief may require. The decree holder must apply for execution within 12 years from date of decree. Arrest in civil prison is only available for decrees for payment of money, not for immoveable property.

section_title: Revision of orders prejudicial to revenue
section_desc: Section 263 ITA: The Commissioner may call for and examine the record of any proceeding under this Act, and if he considers that any order passed therein by the Assessing Officer is erroneous in so far as it is prejudicial to the interests of the revenue, he may, after giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard and after making or causing to be made such inquiry as he deems necessary, pass such order thereon as the circumstances of the case justify.

Section 147 ITA: If the Assessing Officer has reason to believe that any income chargeable to tax has escaped assessment for any assessment year, he may, subject to the provisions of sections 148 to 153, assess or reassess such income and also any other income chargeable to tax which has escaped assessment and which comes to his notice subsequently in the course of the proceedings under this section.

section_title: Interest for defaults in furnishing return of income
section_desc: Section 234A ITA: Where the return of income for any assessment year is furnished after the due date specified under section 139(1) or is not furnished, the assessee shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of one percent for every month or part of a month comprised in the period commencing on the date immediately following the due date and ending on the date of furnishing the return, or where no return has been furnished, on the date of completion of the assessment.

Every supplier shall be liable to be registered under this Act in the State or Union territory from where he makes taxable supply of goods or services or both, if his aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds forty lakh rupees (twenty lakh for special category states). Persons engaged in supply of goods exclusively: forty lakh rupees threshold. Persons engaged in supply of services or both: twenty lakh rupees.

Every registered person, other than an Input Service Distributor, a non-resident taxable person and a person paying tax under sections 10, 51 or 52 shall furnish, electronically, in such form and manner as may be prescribed, the details of outward supplies of goods or services or both effected during a tax period on or before the eleventh day of the month succeeding the said tax period and such details shall be communicated to the recipient of the said supplies.

section_title: Determination of tax not paid or short paid or erroneously refunded or input tax credit wrongly availed or utilised for any reason other than fraud or any wilful misstatement or suppression of facts
section_desc: Section 73 GST: Where it appears to the proper officer that any tax has not been paid or short paid or erroneously refunded, or where input tax credit has been wrongly availed or utilised, he shall serve notice on the person chargeable with tax. The notice must be served within three years from the due date for filing of annual return. If the person pays the demand within 30 days of notice, no penalty shall be imposed.

section_title: Prior registration of real estate project with Real Estate Regulatory Authority
section_desc: No promoter shall advertise, market, book, sell or offer for sale, or invite persons to purchase in any manner any plot, apartment or building, as the case may be, in any real estate project or part of it, in any planning area, without registering the real estate project with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority established under this Act. A promoter shall make an application to the Authority for registration of the real estate project.

A promoter shall, before accepting any advance or deposit from a person, enter into a written agreement for sale with such person. The promoter shall not accept a sum more than ten percent of the cost of the apartment, plot, or building as an advance payment or an application fee, from a person without first entering into a written agreement for sale. The promoter is responsible for obtaining all approvals and certificates of completion.

If the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment, plot or building in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale or fails to complete by the date specified therein, he shall be liable on demand to the allottees, to return the amount received by him in respect thereof with interest at the rate as prescribed. The allottee shall have the option of maintaining the agreement for sale and be paid interest for every month of delay.

Any aggrieved person may file a complaint with the Authority or the adjudicating officer, as the case may be, for any violation or contravention of the provisions of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder against any promoter, allottee or real estate agent, as the case may be. Every complaint shall be dealt with by the Authority in an expeditious manner not later than sixty days.
chapter_title: Functions of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority

section_title: Documents of which registration is compulsory
section_desc: The following documents shall be registered: instruments of gift of immoveable property; other non-testamentary instruments which purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish, whether in present or in future, any right, title or interest, whether vested or contingent, of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards, to or in immoveable property; non-testamentary instruments which acknowledge the receipt or payment of any consideration on account of the creation, declaration, assignment, limitation or extinction of any such right, title or interest; leases of immoveable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and the exemptions contained in Schedule I, the following instruments shall be chargeable with duty of the amount indicated in that Schedule as the proper duty therefor, that is to say: every instrument mentioned in that Schedule which, not having been previously executed by any person, is executed in India on or after the first day of July, 1899; every bill of exchange, cheque, promissory note, bill of lading, letter of credit, policy of insurance, transfer of share, debenture, proxy or receipt executed out of India and relating to property situate or to a matter or thing to be done in India.

section_title: Instruments not duly stamped inadmissible in evidence etc.
section_desc: No instrument chargeable with duty shall be admitted in evidence for any purpose by any person having by law or consent of parties authority to receive evidence, or shall be acted upon, registered or authenticated by any such person or by any public officer, unless such instrument is duly stamped. However, the instrument can be admitted in evidence on payment of the duty and a penalty of ten times the duty (subject to maximum limit).

Whosoever directly or indirectly attempts to indulge or knowingly assists or knowingly is a party or is actually involved in any process or activity connected with the proceeds of crime and projecting it as untainted property shall be guilty of offence of money-laundering. The term 'proceeds of crime' means any property derived or obtained, directly or indirectly, by any person as a result of criminal activity relating to a scheduled offence.

Whoever commits the offence of money-laundering shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine. Where the proceeds of crime involved relate to any offence specified under paragraph 2 of Part A of the Schedule, the punishment may extend to ten years.

section_title: Attachment of property involved in money-laundering
section_desc: Where the Director or any other officer not below the rank of Deputy Director authorised by the Director for the purposes of this section, has reason to believe that any person is in possession of any proceeds of crime, and such proceeds of crime are likely to be concealed, transferred or dealt with in any manner which may result in frustrating any proceedings relating to confiscation of such proceeds of crime, he may, by order in writing, provisionally attach such property for a period not exceeding one hundred and eighty days.

Where the Director or any other officer not below the rank of Deputy Director authorised by the Director, has reason to believe that any person has committed any act which constitutes money-laundering or is in possession of any proceeds of crime or any record relating to money-laundering, has committed any act constituting money-laundering, he may authorise any officer subordinate to him to enter and search any building, place, vessel, vehicle or aircraft where he has reason to believe that such records or proceeds of crime are kept.
chapter_title: Obligations of Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and Intermediaries

section_desc: In this Act: 'authorised person' means an authorised dealer, money changer, offshore banking unit or any other person for the time being authorised under sub-section (1) of section 10 to deal in foreign exchange or foreign securities; 'capital account transaction' means a transaction which alters the assets or liabilities, including contingent liabilities, outside India of persons resident in India or assets or liabilities in India of persons resident outside India; 'current account transaction' means a transaction other than a capital account transaction.

If any person contravenes any provision of this Act, or contravenes any rule, regulation, notification, direction or order issued in exercise of the powers under this Act, or contravenes any condition subject to which an authorisation is issued by the Reserve Bank, he shall, upon adjudication, be liable to a penalty up to thrice the sum involved in such contravention where such sum is quantifiable, or up to two lakh rupees where the amount is not quantifiable, and where such contravention is a continuing one, further penalty which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day after the first day during which the contravention continues.

No enterprise or association of enterprises or person or association of persons shall enter into any agreement in respect of production, supply, distribution, storage, acquisition or control of goods or provision of services, which causes or is likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition within India. Agreements including: fixing purchase or sale price; limiting production; sharing markets; bid rigging; directly or indirectly resulting in bid rigging or collusive bidding, shall be presumed to have an appreciable adverse effect on competition.
chapter_title: Prohibition of Certain Agreements, Abuse of Dominant Position and Regulation of Combinations

section_desc: No enterprise shall abuse its dominant position. There shall be an abuse of dominant position if an enterprise or a group imposes unfair or discriminatory condition in purchase or sale of goods or service; limits or restricts production of goods or provision of services; indulges in practices that deny market access; uses its dominant position in one relevant market to enter into, or protect, other relevant markets.
chapter_title: Prohibition of Certain Agreements, Abuse of Dominant Position and Regulation of Combinations

section_desc: The acquisition of one or more enterprises by one or more persons or merger or amalgamation of enterprises shall be a combination of such enterprises and persons or enterprises, if the total assets of the combined entity are more than rupees two thousand crores in India, or the turnover is more than rupees six thousand crores in India, or globally the combined value exceeds the prescribed threshold. Such combinations exceeding thresholds require prior notification and approval from CCI.
chapter_title: Prohibition of Certain Agreements, Abuse of Dominant Position and Regulation of Combinations

act: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
section_title: Right of child to free and compulsory education
section_desc: Every child of the age of six to fourteen years shall have the right to free and compulsory education in a neighbourhood school till completion of elementary education. No child shall be liable to pay any kind of fee or charges or expenses which may prevent him or her from pursuing and completing elementary education.
chapter_title: Right to Free and Compulsory Education

act: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
section_title: Extent of school's responsibility for free and compulsory education
section_desc: For the purposes of this Act, a school shall provide free and compulsory elementary education to the child admitted. Every private unaided school shall admit not less than twenty-five percent of the strength of class 1 (or pre-school, where applicable) from the children belonging to weaker section and disadvantaged group in the neighbourhood. The State Government shall reimburse these schools for such admissions.
chapter_title: Duties of Appropriate Government, Local Authority and Parents

section_desc: The appropriate Government and local authorities shall ensure that the persons with disabilities enjoy the right to equality, life with dignity, and respect for his or her integrity equally with others. No person with disability shall be discriminated on the basis of disability unless it is shown that the impugned act or omission is a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim.

All educational institutions funded or recognised by appropriate Governments shall provide inclusive education to the children with disabilities and towards that end shall make schools accessible; provide reasonable accommodation according to the individual's requirements; provide necessary support to children with benchmark disabilities free of charge till they attain the age of eighteen years.

section_title: Maintenance of parents and senior citizens
section_desc: A senior citizen including parent who is unable to maintain himself from his own earning or out of the property owned by him, shall be entitled to make an application under section 5 in case of: children failing to maintain their parents; a childless senior citizen failing to maintain himself; a senior citizen (other than parent) with property given to children/relative failing to receive maintenance from them.

An application for maintenance under this Act may be made by a senior citizen or a parent, as the case may be: by the senior citizen or the parent, as the case may be; or if he is incapable, by any other person or organization authorised by him; or by the Tribunal suo motu. The Tribunal shall, after receiving the application, issue a notice to the person responsible for maintaining.

section_title: Power of Central Government to take measures to protect and improve environment
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government shall have the power to take all such measures as it deems necessary or expedient for the purpose of protecting and improving the quality of the environment and preventing, controlling and abating environmental pollution. Such measures include: co-ordinating actions of State Governments; laying down standards; restricting areas for industries; conducting surveys; inspecting premises; establishment or recognition of environmental laboratories; collection of statistics on environment.
chapter_title: General Powers of the Central Government

section_title: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act
section_desc: Whoever fails to comply with or contravenes any of the provisions of this Act, or the rules made or orders or directions issued thereunder, shall, in respect of each such failure or contravention, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both, and in case the failure or contravention continues, with additional fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day during which such failure or contravention continues after the conviction for the first such failure or contravention.

act: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
section_title: Prohibition on use of stream or well for disposal of polluting matter etc.
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall knowingly cause or permit any poisonous, noxious or polluting matter determined in accordance with such standards as may be laid down by the State Board to enter (whether directly or indirectly) into any stream or well; or any other matter which may tend, either directly or in combination with similar matters, to impede the proper flow in the manner leading or likely to lead to a substantial aggravation of pollution due to other causes; or any other matter as may be prescribed by the State Board.
chapter_title: Prevention and Control of Water Pollution

act: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
section_title: Prohibition and restriction on use of certain industrial plants
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall, without the previous consent of the State Board, establish or operate any industrial plant in an air pollution control area. A person intending to establish or operate any industrial plant in an air pollution control area shall make an application in the prescribed form to the State Board for its consent. The Board may grant or refuse consent to establish or operate an industrial plant on such terms and conditions as it may deem fit.
chapter_title: Prevention and Control of Air Pollution

section_desc: The Tribunal shall have the jurisdiction over all civil cases where a substantial question relating to environment (including enforcement of any legal right relating to environment), is involved and such question arises out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I. Such enactments include: Water Act, Air Act, Environment Protection Act, Public Liability Insurance Act, Biological Diversity Act, Forest (Conservation) Act.
chapter_title: Jurisdiction, Powers, and Proceedings of the Tribunal

section_desc: An application for grant of relief or compensation or settlement of dispute may be made to the Tribunal by: the person who has sustained the injury; the owner of the property to which the damage has been caused; where death has resulted from the environmental damage, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased; any aggrieved person including any representative body or organisation. No application shall be entertained if it is not made within a period of six months from the date on which the cause for such application first arose.
chapter_title: Jurisdiction, Powers, and Proceedings of the Tribunal

section_desc: Any person who, in a reserved forest: makes any fresh clearing by felling or burning; sets fire to, or kindles a fire near, any such forest; trespasses or pastures cattle, or permits cattle to trespass; causes any damage by negligence in felling any tree or cutting or dragging any timber; fells, girdles, lops, taps, or burns any tree or strips off the bark or leaves from, or otherwise damages the same; quarries stone, burns lime or charcoal, or collects, subjects to any manufacturing process, or removes any forest-produce; hunts, shoots, fishes, poisons water, or sets traps or snares — shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five hundred rupees or both.

act: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006
section_title: Forest rights of forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers
section_desc: The forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers shall have the following rights: right to hold and live in the forest land under the individual or common occupation for habitation or for self-cultivation for livelihood; community rights such as nistar, by whatever name called; right to own, use, and dispose of minor forest produce; rights for conversion of pattas or leases or grants issued by any local authority or any State Government; right of access to biodiversity.
